predecessors.text: Gandhara and the western Punjab: Apollodotus I became independent of Bactria, ruling from Gandhara and western Punjab (Indo-Greek Kingdom page); the Greco-Bactrian dossier gives the Kabul valley…

successors.name: Indo-Scythians
successors.text: the eastern Punjab around Sagala (Sialkot), Strato II's capital, taken by Rajuvula c.

ledger.x: c. 175: Apollodotus I makes the Indo-Greek Kingdom independent of Bactria. He became independent as 'the first proper Indo-Greek king', ruling from Gandhara and western Punjab, not from Bactria (c. 180/175 on the page). Disagreement: the infobox gives 'c. 200 BCE', the body dates Demetrius I's invasion to about 200…

c. 170: Eucratides of Bactria invades the Indo-Greek lands. He 'seems to have occupied territory as far as the Indus, between ca. 170 BC and 150 BC' (Indo-Greek Kingdom page); the Greco-Bactrian page: he 'campaigned extensively in present-day northwestern India' and his mints reached 'as far as the Jhelum River'.

c. 165: Menander's realm takes shape. The Menander page gives an empire 'from the Kabul River in the west to the Ravi River in the east' and 'from the Swat River valley in the north to Arachosia (the Helmand Province)'; the Indo-Greek Kingdom page has him ruling the Punjab from 165 and dates Indo-Greek control of…

c. 165: Menander I rules from Sagala. 'Thus from 165 BCE until his death in 130 BCE, Menander I ruled Punjab with Sagala as his capital.' The Menander page: 'His capital is supposed to have been Sagala.'

c. 150: Menander pushes Eucratides' dynasty back. The Menander page has him pushing them 'back as far as the Paropamisadae', so Gandhara is Indo-Greek and the Kabul valley stays with the Greco-Bactrian line; the year is the end of the 170-150 span on the Indo-Greek Kingdom page (the Greco-Bactrian page has Eucratides…
c. 150: the fighting over the Kabul valley and Gandhara ends with Eucratides' occupation (ca. 170-150) pushed back by Menander.
Arachosia leaves the kingdom after Menander.

c. 127: Heliocles' holdings south of the Hindu Kush join the Indo-Greek line. The Greco-Bactrian page: he is 'technically the last Greco-Bactrian king' and 'Descendants of Heliocles, moving beyond the Hindu Kush, would form the western part of the Indo-Greek kingdom'; the page has him leaving Bactria for the Kabul…
The rest of Cliopatria's 126 shape (Balochistan, the Khyber edge, Kashmir, the Rajasthan edge: 951 cells) lies outside the realm the Menander I page bounds.
Cliopatria's 110 shape drops the Hindu Kush north slope to the Yuezhi shape.
Cliopatria's 110 shape gives the Ghazni-Zabul country to the Saka.
The southern margin leaves (Sindh and the Rajasthan edge, 176 cells).

c. 80: Maues takes Gandhara and Taxila. 'Maues first conquered Gandhara and Taxila in present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan c. 80 BCE', from the Indo-Greek king Apollodotus II (Indo-Scythians page). Cliopatria's shape loses them in 87. The Apollodotus II page reverses the order ('Apollodotus II took over Taxila after…

c. 80: the Paropamisadae pass from Hermaeus's line to the Yuezhi or Saka. The page has Hermaeus ruling the Paropamisadae until around 80 BCE, with posthumous coins to about 40 CE; the Greco-Bactrian page has the Yuezhi invading his territory about 70 BC. The Yuezhi are named as the counterpart; the page's other…
Cliopatria's last Indo-Greek shape ends in 78 and its Indo-Scythian shape from 77 holds the rest of the land (962 Punjab cells).
Apollodotus II holds the Punjab, Taxila included.
55: Azes I defeats Hippostratos and takes the western Punjab.

c. 10 CE: Rajuvula eliminates Strato II, the last Indo-Greek king, and takes Sagala. 'Rajuvula apparently eliminated Strato II (the last Indo-Greek king) c. 10 CE and took Sagala, his capital city.' The Indo-Greek Kingdom page: Strato II and III 'ruled in the Punjab region until around 10 AD'; infobox 'Disestablished…

wars.name: Eucratides' wars in India
wars.outcome: Eucratides occupied land as far as the Indus between ca.

wars.name: Menander's campaigns towards Mathura and the Ganges
wars.outcome: Accounts name Sakala, Mathura, Panchala and Saketa and possibly Pataliputra; Patanjali describes a failed campaign as far as Mathura.

wars.name: Yuezhi and Saka pressure on the Greek lands north and west of the Hindu Kush
wars.outcome: Ai-Khanoum burnt about 145; eastern Scythians invaded Bactria from about 140 and the Yuezhi expanded south around 120; Heliocles left Bactria for the Kabul valley and the Greek kingdom of Bactria ended (infobox c.

wars.name: Maues's conquest of Gandhara and Taxila
wars.outcome: Maues took Gandhara and Taxila from Apollodotus II c.

wars.name: Azes I's conquest of north-western India
wars.outcome: Azes I defeated Hippostratos in 55 BCE and the Indo-Scythians took control of north-western India; the eastern Punjab stayed Indo-Greek.

wars.name: Rajuvula's conquest of Sagala
wars.outcome: Rajuvula eliminated Strato II, the last Indo-Greek king, c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on any opened page; the frontiers are rivers (the Indus, the Ravi, the Helmand) and city-states approximated by regions, and the coins that fix the reigns do not fix borders.
